title: Look East for Lessons in Democratic Resistance
gist: Pro-democracy movements look to Eastern/Central Europe for inspiration while overlooking East Asia's democratic breakthroughs, even though a country in the region recently reversed authoritarian drift by ousting a would-be dictator, offering an underused playbook for resisting autocracy.

insights.claim: Pro-democracy activists disproportionately draw inspiration from Eastern and Central Europe's history, while East Asia's own significant democratic breakthroughs receive far less attention despite offering comparable lessons.
insights.speaker: Jeffrey N. Wasserstrom
insights.so_what: Suggests analysts and risk-watchers tracking authoritarian-to-democratic transitions should widen their comparative frameworks to include East Asian cases, not just the post-1989 European template.
insights.quote: Pro-democracy activists often turn to Eastern and Central Europe for inspiration, while Asia’s remarkable democratic breakthroughs receive far less attention.

insights.claim: Sixty years ago, harsh autocratic rule dominated a region at the eastern edge of a continent, yet within decades competitive elections became the norm and former political prisoners went on to lead governments.
insights.speaker: Jeffrey N. Wasserstrom
insights.so_what: Provides a historical base rate showing durable authoritarian regimes can transition to competitive democracies within a single generation, relevant for long-horizon political-risk modeling in Asia.
insights.quote: Sixty years ago, harsh autocratic rule dominated a region at the eastern edge of a continent. Quixotic quests for political change seemed to have little chance of succeeding—until they did.

insights.claim: Voters in one East Asian country recently reversed years of authoritarian drift by joining forces to oust a would-be dictator, despite the region's recent democratic setbacks.
insights.speaker: Jeffrey N. Wasserstrom
insights.so_what: Signals that recent authoritarian backsliding in parts of East Asia is not one-directional and can be reversed through organized civic/electoral resistance, a relevant precedent for regional political-risk assessment.
insights.quote: Despite recent setbacks, voters in one of these countries just reversed years of authoritarian drift, joining forces to oust a would-be dictator.

insights.claim: East Asia's recent political struggles offer valuable lessons for those seeking to resist the global advance of authoritarianism.
insights.speaker: Jeffrey N. Wasserstrom
insights.so_what: Frames East Asian democratic resistance movements as a template worth studying amid a broader global trend of democratic backsliding.
insights.quote: the continent’s recent struggles offer valuable lessons for those seeking to resist the global advance of authoritarianism
